title: Baraat Vendor Record
description: The structured shape every messy vendor doc must resolve to after extraction. This is the machine-checkable contract; see vendor_schema_spec.md for plain-language rationale, worked examples, and cross-field rules that JSON Schema cannot express on its own.

vendor_id.description: Stable unique id, derived from the source filename slug.

name.description: Business name exactly as it appears in the doc.

category.description: One of the five fixed vendor categories.

price_range_inr.description: Best current price estimate in INR. max may be null for open-ended 'and up' pricing. Cross-field rule (enforced in code): if both present, min <= max.

price_unit.description: What the price is measured per. Cross-field rule (enforced in code): caterer => per_plate; venue => per_day; photographer/decorator/makeup_artist => package or per_event.

price_last_verified.description: Date the price was last known good (YYYY-MM-DD), or null when no date is given or the price is stale.

price_confidence.description: high = single uncontested current price; low = single but vague/undated/open-ended; stale = conflicting figures across dates or an explicit old 'as of' marker.

gst_number.description: 15-char GST id if stated in the doc, else null. Never invent one: if the doc has no GST, this MUST be null.

red_flags.description: Problems found (complaints, disputes, quality issues). Empty array if none — never omitted.

source_file.description: Filename this record was extracted from (attribution).

needs_human_review.description: True only when validation could not be satisfied after repair attempts. NOTE: a stale price is NOT a human-review case — that is a successfully handled state.

extraction_notes.description: Human-readable note explaining staleness, open-ended pricing, or why human review was flagged. Cross-field rule (enforced in code): if needs_human_review is true, this MUST be non-null.
